clue.text: Traitor in Paris who attracts support

parts.note: qui is French for who
a sling supports an injured arm

explanation.surface: A collaborator in occupied Paris draws people to back him.
explanation.definitionFit: Vidkun Quisling's name became a byword for a collaborator who betrays his own country.

clue.text: Crucial-sounding place for loading and unloading ships

definitions.text: place for loading and unloading ships

indicators.note: sounding means it is heard rather than seen, so the word for crucial is said out loud

parts.note: key means crucial, as in a key point

explanation.surface: A vital-sounding spot where ships are loaded and unloaded.
explanation.definitionFit: A quay is a stone wharf where vessels berth to load cargo.

clue.text: Affair producing children?

definitions.meaning: a matter or affair under discussion

explanation.surface: An extramarital fling results in children.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Affair' looks romantic, but here it is a matter for debate.
explanation.definitionFit: Issue is a topic of concern and also, in legal language, a person's offspring.

clue.text: Transparency islander lent freely

indicators.note: freely suggests letters moving without restriction, so these are rearranged

explanation.surface: An island dweller generously lent out some see-through film.
explanation.definitionFit: A lantern slide is a glass photographic plate projected by a magic lantern, an early transparency.

clue.text: Reportedly worked flour into dough, as required

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard, so the baking word is spoken aloud

parts.note: kneaded means worked dough with the hands

explanation.surface: A baker worked the dough as the recipe demanded.
explanation.definitionFit: Needed and required both mean necessary.

clue.text: Type of seabird others rejected

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so the word for the others is read backwards

parts.note: auks are other seabirds, different from the one defined

explanation.surface: A kind of seabird is shunned by the rest of the flock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'others' means other seabirds: AUKS, read backwards for 'rejected'.
explanation.definitionFit: The skua is a predatory gull-like bird of northern seas.

clue.text: Giving birth on farm? — not being serious!

definitions.meaning: a goat ... gives birth to kids

explanation.definitionFit: Kidding is a goat producing young and also joking around.

clue.text: Caucasian soldiers initially installed in Irish islands

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so these pieces go within the islands

parts.note: the Aran Islands lie off Galway in Ireland
men means soldiers, the ranks

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word it qualifies

explanation.surface: White troops are stationed first on islands off Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Caucasian' looks like a racial term, but here it means from the Caucasus region.
explanation.definitionFit: Armenia lies in the Caucasus, so an Armenian is a Caucasian person.

clue.text: Breaks rest to develop a mode of swimming

indicators.note: develop means grow into something new, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A swimmer stops resting and works up a stroke.
explanation.definitionFit: Breaststroke is a swimming style with a frog-like kick.

clue.text: Member of clergy beheaded for crime

indicators.note: beheaded means the head, the first letter, of the clergyman's title comes off

parts.note: a parson is a parish priest

explanation.surface: A clergyman is executed for an offence.
explanation.definitionFit: Deliberately setting fire to property is a criminal offence.

clue.text: A model unexpectedly receiving right noble rank

indicators.note: receiving means the jumbled letters take another piece inside them
unexpectedly suggests things turning out differently, so the letters of a model are rearranged

explanation.surface: A fashion model is surprisingly elevated to the peerage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unexpectedly' scrambles A MODEL to EALDOM, and 'receiving' puts R inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: An earldom is the title and status held by an earl, a peer's rank.

clue.text: Decline of French people of similar age

parts.note: de is French for of
a generation is everyone born around the same time

explanation.surface: The French complain about the decay of their own age group.
explanation.definitionFit: Degeneration is a falling off in quality or condition, a decline.

clue.text: She plays a series of jazz chords for law officers

parts.words: plays a series of jazz chords
parts.note: to riff is to play repeated short jazz phrases

explanation.surface: A jazz musician performs for policemen.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheriffs are law-enforcement officers, especially in US counties.

clue.text: Going to ground, getting beating

definitions.meaning: going to ground means taking cover

explanation.surface: A fugitive goes to ground while taking a beating.
explanation.definitionFit: Hiding is both concealment from pursuers and an informal word for a thrashing.

clue.text: Noblewoman's daughter beginning to understand board game

indicators.note: beginning to points to the opening letter of the next word

parts.note: chess is a board game

explanation.surface: A lady's daughter starts to understand a board game.
explanation.definitionFit: A duchess is a woman with the rank of duke, a high noble title.

clue.text: , Greek character concealing source of this disgrace

indicators.note: concealing means the Greek letter holds another piece hidden inside it

parts.note: sigma is a letter of the Greek alphabet

indicators.note: the source of a word is where it starts, its opening letter

explanation.surface: A Greek figure is hiding where this shame came from.
explanation.definitionFit: A stigma is a mark of social shame attached to someone.

clue.text: One who endures being a carrier of equipment?

definitions.meaning: a ... bears, puts up with, hardship
a ... carries loads, as on safari

explanation.surface: Someone who puts up with being an equipment porter.
explanation.definitionFit: Bearer is one who bears, in the senses of tolerating and carrying.

clue.text: Memory concerning offertory

parts.note: re means concerning or about
the offertory is the collection taken in church

explanation.surface: Someone remembers something about the church collection.
explanation.definitionFit: A recollection is something recalled, a memory.

clue.text: Senior citizen taken in by soldiers

indicators.note: taken in by means held within the next word, so the answer is concealed there

explanation.surface: An elderly person is conned by troops.
explanation.definitionFit: An oldie is an informal term for an elderly person.

clue.text: Cook disturbed by a noisy quarrel

indicators.note: disturbed by means broken into, so the cooking word is split open by the next piece

parts.note: to fry is to cook

explanation.surface: A chef is interrupted by a loud argument.
explanation.definitionFit: A fray is a brawl or noisy fight.

clue.text: Condition backed by more senior cricketer, perhaps

indicators.note: by means placed beside, so the older word follows
backed means turned back, so the word for condition is read backwards

parts.note: if introduces a condition
elder means older, more senior

explanation.surface: A condition is supported by an older cricketer.
explanation.definitionFit: A fielder is a player on the fielding side in cricket or baseball, hence 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Instruction to supply goods called for by the Speaker?

definitions.meaning: a request for goods from a supplier
the Speaker of the House of Commons calls '...!' to restore calm

explanation.surface: An instruction to deliver goods is requested by whoever is speaking.
explanation.walkthrough: The Speaker is the chair of Britain's House of Commons, who shouts 'Order!' when MPs get rowdy.
explanation.definitionFit: An order is both a purchase request and the call for decorum in parliament.

clue.text: Symbol of rank crack troops held at first

parts.note: the SAS, the Special Air Service, is the British army's elite special forces regiment

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: Elite soldiers hold a badge of rank from the outset.
explanation.definitionFit: A sash worn across the chest can mark an office or order of chivalry.

clue.text: Lines by English novelist identifying vegetation

indicators.note: by means placed beside, so lines follow the novelist

parts.note: Graham Greene was an English novelist
RY, railway, is the crossword abbreviation for lines

explanation.surface: Lines by an English writer pick out the plant life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lines by' reads as verse written by the novelist, but the lines are railway lines.
explanation.definitionFit: Greenery is green foliage or plants collectively.
